overview.body:
**Radagast** ​(*radagast*) ‌— Hospitality, ‌Animals ​· ​Council ​of the ​gods ​— ‌belongs ​to the ​Slavic ‌tradition, ​where it ‌is ​catalogued ‌under ​the domain ​"Hospitality, ​Animals". ​The ​name means ‌"Council ​of ‌the ​gods".

**Radagast** ‌is ​hospitality, ‌animals. ​The name ‌means ​"Council ​of ‌the gods" ‌and ‌belongs ​to the ​slavic ‌tradition.

​PuniCodex ​restores the ‌name ​as ​**Radagast** ‌and serves ​its ‌temple ​at ​[its temple](https://punicodex.com/radagast/). ​The ​restoration ‌needs ‌no distinctive ​letters ‌or ​diacritics its ​ASCII ‌form ‌would ‌lose, which ‌places ​the ‌name ​in Tier ​2. ​The ‌plain ​ASCII form ​*radagast* ​survives ‌as ​a modern ​convenience ​imposed ‌by ​the early ‌domain-name ​system; ‌the restoration, ​not ‌the ‌fallback, ​is the ​form ​the ​project ‌defends as ‌philologically ​complete.

the-name.body:
No ​indigenous written ‌attestation ‌survives for ​this name; ​**Radagast** ​is a ​scholarly ​transliteration of ‌the reconstructed ​spoken ​form. Etymologically ‌the ​name means ‌"Council ​of the ‌gods".

The ​ASCII ​form *radagast* ​survives ​only because ​the ‌early domain-name ​system could ‌not ​carry diacritics; ‌it ​is a ‌technological compromise, ​not ‌an ancient ​spelling. ​The Unicode ‌restoration ‌**Radagast** recovers ‌the full ​diacritic ​detail of ‌the ​scholarly transliteration ​directly ‌in the ​address bar. ​The ‌restoration needs ​no ‌distinctive letters ​or diacritics ​its ​ASCII form ​would ‌lose, which ‌places ​the name ‌in Tier ​2.

​The letter-by-letter ‌transformation ‌runs:

- ‌**r** ‌→ **R** ​— Same
‌- ​**a** → ​**a** ​— Same
‌- **d** ​→ ​**d** — ​Same
‌- **a** ​→ ​**a** — ​Same
- ‌**g** ​→ **g** ‌— ​Same
- ‌**a** ​→ **a** ‌— Same
‌- ​**s** → ​**s** ​— Same
​- **t** ‌→ ‌**t** — ​Same

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/radagast/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**radagast** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Radagast.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"radagast" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Radagast".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"radagast" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Radagast" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Radagast was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Radagast ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌Radagast ‌place ​hospitality, animals ​at ​the center ​of ​a ‌living mythological ​world.

​### ‌Origins (Myth)

​Radagast ‌appears in ​slavic ‌tradition ​as hospitality, ​animals. ​The name's ​meaning, ​"Council ‌of the ​gods", ‌shapes ​the narratives ‌told ​about this ‌figure.

​### ‌Worship and ​Memory ​(Cult)

Devotees ‌and ‌later ‌tradition-keepers preserved ​Radagast ​in ‌ritual, text, ​and ​iconography, ensuring ‌the ​name ​survived into ‌the ​modern scholarly ‌record.

​The ​myths of ​Radagast ​survive in ‌fragments, ‌summaries, ​and later ‌retellings. ​Each ​version reflects ‌the ‌interests of ‌its ‌tellers ​— poets, ‌priests, ​philosophers, and ​scholars. ​The ‌PuniCodex entry ​does ​not ​privilege a ‌single ​version; it ​gathers ​the ‌attestations so ​that ‌readers can ​compare ‌them. ​The restoration ‌Radagast ‌gives ​the figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Radagast ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Slavic ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌Radagast, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​hospitality ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

meditation.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Radagast is ‌to ​hold ​the ​idea of ​hospitality, ​Animals ‌in ​the mind ​and ‌to ​ask ‌what ​of it ‌endures. ​The ​name ​means "Council ​of ​the ‌gods" ​— and ‌a ​name ‌that ​carries its ‌meaning ​so ‌openly ​invites meditation ​rather ‌than ‌mere ‌recollection. ​The tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name ​as hospitality, ‌Animals ​· ​Council ‌of the ​gods.

‌Sit ​with ​the restored ​form ​— ‌Radagast ‌— and ​the ‌diacritics ​themselves ​become ‌the practice: ‌each ‌mark ‌is ​a small ‌act ​of ​attention, ​a refusal ‌to ​let ​the ​plain ASCII ‌form ​*radagast* ​stand ​in for ‌the ​whole. ‌What ​the ‌tradition preserved ​in ‌this ‌name, ​the restoration ​asks ​the ​reader ‌to preserve ‌in ​turn.
